member.name: T:NetSync.Peers.PeerProtocol
member.summary:
Peer-level messages, carried inside transport Data payloads.
Handshake (plaintext): Hello [0x01][ver=3][token:8][configHash:4][keyExchange:1][suites:1][pubLen:1][pub…][cookieLen:1][cookie…] — client introduces itself on every link; the token groups the links into one connection, configHash covers the channel table and MaxMessageSize, suites is the bitmask of cipher suites the client can run. Welcome [0x02][connectionId:8][suite:1][pubLen:1][pub…][idLen:1][identityKey…][sigLen:1][signature…] — server bound the link; ECDH public key, and when the server has an identity its public key plus a signature over the handshake transcript. Reject [0x03][reason:1] — handshake refused (version/encryption/config/auth). Retry [0x06][cookie:16] — UDP-only servers: prove your address, resend Hello with this cookie.
Session (inside the authenticated envelope on encrypted connections): Join [0x07][connectData…] — client: open the connection (data encrypted when keyed). JoinAccept [0x08] — server: connection open. JoinReject [0x09][reason utf8…] — server application refused. Bye [0x04][reason:1] — graceful disconnect notice. Degrade [0x05] — client (on TCP): "UDP failed, carry my UDP channels over TCP". TimeReq [0x0A][clientTime:8] — client: what time is it on the server? TimeResp [0x0B][clientTime:8][serverTime:8] — server: echo + its clock (double ms, bit pattern BE). PathMtu [0x0C][datagramSize:2] — client: the measured path MTU; use it for fragments too. Data [0x10][channel:1][payload…] — application data. RelData / RelAck — reliability layer (see ReliableEndpoint). Secure [0x40][counter:8][tag:16][inner…] — authenticated envelope (see LinkSecurity).

member.name: T:NetSync.Pipeline.Reliability.CongestionWindow
member.summary:
Per-channel congestion window, in packets in flight.
Loss-based (Normal/High): Reno-style — slow start to ssthresh, then +1 packet per RTT; a loss event halves the window at most once per RTT.
Delay-based (Low): LEDBAT-style scavenger — grows only while the queueing delay it observes stays under and shrinks as soon as it exceeds it, so bulk transfers soak up idle capacity but yield to real-time channels the moment a queue starts forming. member.name: T:NetSync.Pipeline.Reliability.ReliableEndpoint
member.summary:
Reliability engine for one unreliable datagram link (ENet-style ARQ with TCP-grade congestion control). One instance per datagram link; transport-agnostic — it only needs a send delegate.
Per channel, depending on : - 16-bit wrap-aware sequence numbers and a 256-packet range window, - ACKs carrying a 32-packet history bitmask: immediate, or — on links that report datagram boundaries () — one per channel per received datagram, sent together with the replies to it, - RTO from ACK-sampled SRTT/RTTVAR (Karn's rule), exponential backoff, - fast retransmit after 3 later packets were acked (loss recovered in ~1 RTT), - congestion window per channel: Reno-style, or delay-based scavenger for channels, - duplicate elimination and (ReliableOrdered) reorder buffering, - fragmentation above (1100 B, raised to fit the path MTU once measured), reliable or unreliable.
Threading: HandleRelData/HandleAck are called from the link's receive thread; Send* may be called from any thread; retransmission timers run on the shared thread (). Sender state is guarded by a per-channel lock (then the RTT lock — always in that order); receiver state is only touched by the receive thread.
Memory: every packet lives in a pooled buffer. A pending packet's buffer can be read by a (re)transmission outside the lock while an ACK removes it, so it goes back to the pool only when no send is reading it (PendingPacket.InFlight). The send delegate must consume the bytes before it returns (all NetSync links do). Delivered payloads are valid only during the deliver callback.

member.name: T:NetSync.Pipeline.Security.ConnectionCrypto
member.summary:
Per-connection key material and the payload cipher, for one side (client or server) of one connection.
Every key is per direction (client→server, server→client): a peer never encrypts or authenticates with the key it verifies with, so its own packets can't be reflected back to it, and GCM nonces can't collide between directions.
Payload encryption only provides confidentiality on top of an already authenticated packet: every post-handshake packet travels in a envelope whose tag covers the ciphertext. Hence: - AesCbcHmacSha256: [iv:16][ciphertext] — no second MAC (the envelope's HMAC is it). - AesGcm: [nonce:12][tag:16][ciphertext] — GCM's own tag comes for free. Both are allocation-free on net8.0; netstandard2.1 runs CBC through the classic transform API, which allocates per message.

member.name: T:NetSync.Pipeline.Security.LinkSecurity
member.summary:
Authenticates every post-handshake packet on one link of an encrypted connection.
Envelope: [MsgSecure:1][counter:8 BE][tag:16][inner peer message…] - AesCbcHmacSha256: tag = HMAC-SHA256(directionKey, slot ‖ counter ‖ inner)[0..16] - AesGcm: tag = GMAC(directionKey, nonce = slot ‖ 0 0 0 ‖ counter, aad = inner)
This closes what payload encryption alone leaves open: the inner message's header — channel, flags, sequence number, and whole ACK/Bye/Degrade messages — is covered by the tag, so it can't be forged (e.g. fake ACKs that make a "reliable" channel lose data) or moved between links/channels. The 64-bit counter plus a 1024-packet sliding window rejects replays, while still accepting the reordering UDP produces. Confidentiality stays per channel (Encryption flag).
Thread-safety: Wrap may be called from any thread (counter and MAC under a lock); Unwrap is called only from the link's receive thread. Allocation-free: incremental MACs into stack buffers, envelopes in pooled buffers.

member.name: T:NetSync.Sending.SendQueue
member.summary:
Priority send queue with a dedicated drain loop.
- Wakes exactly when work arrives, without allocating (). After an idle period the first write happens on the enqueuing thread itself. - Optional coalescing: consecutive small frames are copied into one pooled batch and written with a single socket call — far fewer syscalls under load, while a lone message still goes out immediately (no Nagle-style delay). - Bounded: fails fast when full (real-time traffic), waits for space (bulk transfers — backpressure instead of failing halfway through a file). Bulk is additionally capped in bytes, so streaming a huge file holds only a few MB in the queue. - Pooled buffers are returned after the write, or when the queue shuts down. - lets the owner detect a write that never completes (remote stopped reading) on every runtime, including ones where socket writes ignore cancellation.

member.name: T:NetSync.Transports.Udp.DatagramBatcher
member.summary:
Packs small UDP packets into shared datagrams — one socket call carries many messages.
Callers only copy their packet into the destination's open batch; one drain loop per transport sends the batches. While that loop is inside a socket call, new packets keep accumulating, so batching grows with load on its own and never delays a lone packet (no timer, no Nagle-style wait). A batch holding a single packet goes out as a plain Data datagram — the receiver sees exactly the pre-batching wire format.
Wire format of a batch: [Batch][len][packet][len][packet]… where len is a 1–3 byte little-endian base-128 varint and each packet is the payload of a Data datagram. A batch never exceeds (below the IPv6 minimum MTU, so it is never IP-fragmented); larger packets go out alone, in order with the batched ones.
The receive thread corks the batcher while it handles one datagram (/): everything it sends in response — acks, replies — leaves together once the datagram is done, instead of the drain loop waking halfway and splitting it. Other threads are never held back by the cork.
Bounded: a destination holds at most ; beyond that new packets are dropped, exactly like a full socket buffer drops them (the reliability layer retransmits what matters).

member.summary:
WebSocket transport for the slot — the way browsers (WebAssembly, Blazor) and networks that only let HTTP(S) through reach a NetSync server. The whole stack runs on top unchanged: channels, handshake, encryption, approval.
Server: server.AddListener(TransportType.Tcp, new WebSocketTransportFactory(), 8080) next to the native TCP/UDP listeners — both kinds of clients share one server. Give it a for wss:// (required by pages served over https).
Client: config.TransportFactories[TransportType.Tcp] = new WebSocketTransportFactory { UseTls = true, HostName = "game.example.com" }. Where UDP is unavailable (browsers), UDP channels automatically ride the WebSocket ( = false).
Wire format: one binary WebSocket message per packet, [type:1][payload] — the same packets as UDP; messages of 64 KB and more are sent as fragments so small traffic never waits behind a file.
